correctness.rationale: Published Proposition 4.1 gives square iff gcd(h,u_n)=1 and pairwise coprime iterated numerators under (u,v)->(u^2+v^2,uv). For each p^alpha||h, initial ratio mod p has an absorbing pole unless v_p(x0)=alpha. In the equality case the ratio equals (x0/p^alpha)*(h/p^alpha)^(-1) mod p and iterates by T(t)=t+t^(-1) until a unique zero hit. Every finite-field hit t gives exactly one x0 class modulo p^(alpha+1). p=3 mod4 cannot hit because predecessor solves t^2=-1; p=2 is included. CRT independence across primes yields exact period and collision-aware distribution. Independent code checked 8147 local starting residues across h<=36 and h=65, including direct integer (u_n,v_n) failure indices for h<=21 and h=65; the h65 counts match 3507/714/4. h=1 empty product M=1 yields all starts zero failures.

final_claim: For every fixed positive h and starting integer x0, the failure indices of the reciprocal-sum square test are the distinct finite first-hitting times to 0 for t->t+1/t at primes p|h with p=2 or 1 mod 4, activated only when v_p(x0)=v_p(h); this gives periodicity modulo product p^(v_p(h)+1) and an exact CRT density formula grouping simultaneous prime hits. At h=65, counts are 3507,714,4 modulo 4225.
